layers.process: You need your passport to travel between Peninsular Malaysia and Sabah, even though the trip stays inside Malaysia. East Malaysia (Sabah and Sarawak) has its own entry checks.

layers.authority: Malaysian security authorities and police in the Eastern Sabah Security Zone (ESSZone); the Sabah Government restricts use of the waterways
layers.process: A 6 pm to 6 am curfew on water travel applies in 6 coastal districts of eastern Sabah, including waters up to 3 nautical miles (5.5 km) offshore. In daylight, vessels in the waters off Lahad Datu and Sandakan need a permit or permission from police, and all vessels must keep to designated routes. Resort-run water activities at night, including diving and fishing, are banned. Authorities may extend the curfew each fortnight; travelling by water in curfew hours without permission can bring a fine or up to 6 months' jail. The ESSZone covers Beluran, Kinabatangan, Kota Marudu, Kudat, Kunak, Lahad Datu, Pitas, Sandakan, Semporna and Tawau.

Sipadan Island Park, international visitors: conservation fee RM100 a person (about A$35.05) and scuba diving fee RM350 (A$122.68). The page says fees can vary by activity and visitor type. A$ at RBA 30 Oct 2026: A$1 = MYR 2.853.

Diving at Sipadan runs on booked permits. Sabah Parks decides permit issue and availability. Registered dive operators can book up to six months ahead at the Sabah Parks head office in Kota Kinabalu or the park office in Semporna, with a 50% deposit, one booking list per dive date, and full payment two weeks before. Cancelling more than two weeks before keeps 10% of the fees; cancelling later forfeits everything paid. No accommodation has been allowed on the island since it became a marine park in 2004. The page gives no daily cap.

Tunku Abdul Rahman Park (off Kota Kinabalu), non-Malaysian entrance per person per day: RM25 for 18 and over (about A$8.76), RM20 for 17 and under or 60 and over (A$7.01). Kuraman scuba diving fee RM200 for international visitors (A$70.10), which the page marks as needing confirmation with the park. A$ at RBA 30 Oct 2026: A$1 = MYR 2.853.

Tawau Hills Park: Sabah Parks lists an international conservation fee of RM20 per adult and RM12 for visitors 17 and under (about A$7.01 and A$4.21 per person at the RBA rate of A$1 = MYR 2.853 on 30 October 2026). The fee includes the botanical garden. Check the current amount and payment arrangements with the park.

Tawau Hills Park: climbing Mount Maria, Mount Lucia or Mount Magdalena requires a climbing permit and registration with Sabah Parks before the climb. The park says to allow at least two days for the mountain outing; check the route and present access with the authority.
Tawau Hills Park: the park says a guide is compulsory for the mountain trail and that guides and the climbing permit should be arranged with Sabah Parks before the climb. A porter is optional.

Tawau Hills Park: Sabah Parks lists an international climbing permit of RM50 per adult or RM20 per visitor 17 and under for one peak (about A$17.53 or A$7.01 at the RBA rate of A$1 = MYR 2.853 on 30 October 2026); the park lists different multiple-peak prices. Climbing insurance and guide charges are separate. Confirm current charges, category and route with the park.

Mount Tambuyukon, Kinabalu Park: Sabah Parks lists a climbing permit for international visitors and separate guide and porter services. The page lists the international climbing permit as RM300 per person per day (about A$105.15 at A$1 = MYR 2.853, RBA 30 October 2026). Confirm route availability, expedition duration, mandatory services and final total with Sabah Parks.

Mount Nambuyukon, Kinabalu Park: Sabah Parks lists an international climbing permit of RM100 per adult and RM40 per visitor 17 and under (about A$35.05 and A$14.02 at A$1 = MYR 2.853, RBA 30 October 2026), with guide and other services listed separately. The park says the route introduction will be updated: ask Serinsim staff to confirm availability and current conditions.

Mount Kinabalu: Sabah Parks lists 20 places per day at Lemaing Hostel for Malaysian citizens and 30 per day at Panalaban Hostel for Malaysian and international climbers. Packages include a climbing permit, insurance, one night and meals; conservation, guide and transport charges are separate. Dates are subject to availability and may change.

Mount Kinabalu: Sabah Parks states one mountain guide for every five adult climbers, or two climbers aged 15 or under. Confirm the guide arrangement for a mixed-age group directly with the park before booking; guide charges are separate from the hostel package.

Mount Kinabalu: Sabah Parks lists climbing insurance as part of its two-day hostel packages; the conservation fee, guide, transport and optional porter are separate. Check what cover applies to the actual trip and any extension with Sabah Parks before payment.

Crocker Range Park: Sabah Parks lists an international conservation fee per person per day of RM20 for adults and RM12 for visitors 17 and under (about A$7.01 and A$4.21 at the RBA rate of A$1 = MYR 2.853 on 30 October 2026). Confirm current charges and opening conditions with the park.

Crocker Range Park: Sabah Parks lists a Rafflesia blooming observation charge for international visitors of RM30 per person per day (about A$10.52 at A$1 = MYR 2.853, RBA 30 October 2026). Blooms are not guaranteed; ask the park about current conditions and applicable admission charges.

Crocker Range Park: Sabah Parks lists an international Minduk Sirung Trail climbing fee of RM100 per adult or RM50 for visitors 17 and under (about A$35.05 or A$17.53 at A$1 = MYR 2.853, RBA 30 October 2026). The page lists insurance and mountain guide charges separately; confirm route access, required services and the total with the park.

Crocker Range Park: Sabah Parks lists an international Mount Tinutudan climbing fee of RM100 per adult or RM50 for visitors 17 and under (about A$35.05 or A$17.53 at A$1 = MYR 2.853, RBA 30 October 2026). The page lists insurance and guide charges separately; confirm the route, required services and total with the park.

Crocker Range Park Salt Trail: Sabah Parks lists a route fee for international visitors of RM100 per adult or RM50 for visitors 17 and under (about A$35.05 or A$17.53 at A$1 = MYR 2.853, RBA 30 October 2026). The published table lists insurance and guide charges separately. Check route access, local arrangements and current prices with the park.

Pulau Tiga Park: Sabah Parks lists an international conservation fee per day of RM20 per adult and RM12 for visitors 17 and under (about A$7.01 and A$4.21 at the RBA rate of A$1 = MYR 2.853 on 30 October 2026). Confirm access and applicable charges with the park.

Pulau Tiga Park: Sabah Parks lists an international volcanic mud bath fee of RM10 per person for the first three hours and RM10 per person for subsequent hours (about A$3.51 for each stated charge at A$1 = MYR 2.853, RBA 30 October 2026). Check how the time charge is applied, current access and total cost with the park.

Sabah Parks explains that section 48 of the Parks Enactment restricts commercial filming, video and still photography in a park or nature reserve unless acting for, or with written permission from, the Board, Director or an authorised park officer. Confirm the location and intended use with Sabah Parks.

Sabah Parks explains that section 48 restricts research and collection of scientific, social or cultural data in a park or nature reserve, with or without specimens, unless acting for or with written permission from the Board, Director or an authorised park officer. Check community and other permissions separately.

Sabah Parks explains that entering park or nature reserve areas other than those developed for public use requires written permission, subject to the enactment and its exceptions. Ask the park authority about the specific route and access conditions.

Sabah Parks summarises section 48 as restricting bringing in or possessing a boat, weapons, traps or specimen-collecting equipment inside a park or nature reserve without the relevant written permission. Boat operators and researchers should check the intended equipment and local permit conditions with the park.

zone-requirements.note: Sabah and Sarawak keep their own immigration powers under Part VII of Malaysia's Immigration Act 1959/63 (the Act wasn't read on an official page).

laws.rule: Sabah and Sarawak keep their own immigration control under the Immigration Act 1959/63: travelling between the Peninsula, Sabah and Sarawak needs a valid passport (no visa), and you clear immigration again on arrival.

Climbing Mount Kinabalu needs a booked package from Sabah Parks (online only; accommodation, permit and insurance are paid at booking). Climbers go with a park mountain guide: Sabah Parks lists one guide for up to five adults or two climbers aged 15 or under, at RM350 per guide (about A$122.68), paid in cash. Names cannot be changed after booking and cancellations are non-refundable. As at 19 September 2026, bookings for the 2027 season had not opened; that dated notice does not confirm current availability. Listed 2026 international rates: climbing permit RM400 adult or RM200 for 17 and under (about A$140.20 or A$70.10) and conservation fee RM50 or RM25 (about A$17.53 or A$8.76), with guide and transport extra. AUD uses the RBA rate of A$1 = MYR 2.853 on 30 October 2026.
laws.penalty_signal: Sabah Parks shared a news report (The Star, September 2026) of a foreign climber fined RM25,000 for illegal entry into Mount Kinabalu. The fine is from a news report, so treat it as a signal.
laws.note: Guide ratio and currency conversions amended 8 November from the Sabah Parks guide search-index snapshot; original review date and earlier news-report penalty signal retained.

laws.rule: Sipadan Island Park: diving needs a permit booked through Sabah Parks (usually by a registered dive operator), and Sabah Parks makes the final decision on availability. International conservation fee RM100 and scuba fee RM350 a person (about A$35.05 and A$122.68; RBA 30 Oct 2026, A$1 = MYR 2.853).
laws.heading: Sabah Parks

laws.rule: For Sabah parks and nature reserves, Sabah Parks summarises section 48 of the Parks Enactment as restricting damage to trees, protected plants and living or dead coral without the relevant written permission, subject to the enactment and its exceptions.

Sabah Parks states that hunting, capturing, injuring or disturbing animals and taking or destroying eggs or nests in parks and nature reserves is restricted without the relevant written permission under section 48; check the enactment and lawful exceptions.

Sabah Parks states that introducing animals or vegetation, permitting a domestic animal to enter or stray, and removing animals or vegetation, alive or dead, are restricted in parks and nature reserves without the relevant written permission under section 48.

Sabah Parks says removing minerals or objects of geological, prehistoric, archaeological, historical or scientific interest from parks and nature reserves is restricted without the relevant written permission under section 48.
Sabah Parks says a fire that endangers a park can be an offence even when it is started outside the park; its summary refers to section 58C. Check local fire restrictions before travelling.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Dress modestly, especially at places of worship. Remove shoes before entering mosques and homes. Don't point with your index finger. A handshake is generally fine. At Kota Kinabalu City Mosque all visitors must register, wear the coverall provided (rental RM 5 to RM 10, about A$1.75 to about A$3.51 at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026), bring no food or drink and not pose inappropriately in photos.
culture-and-protocol.sacred_or_restricted_places: At the City Mosque, observe off-limit areas and don't imitate prayer. Entry RM 5; closed Fridays.
